stem: A factory makes phone chargers on two machines. Machine X makes 60% of the chargers, and machine Y makes the rest. Of the chargers made by machine X, 3% are defective, and of the chargers made by machine Y, 5% are defective. If a defective charger from this factory is selected at random, what is the probability that it was made by machine Y?
solution: Imagine 1,000 chargers: machine X makes 600 and machine Y makes 400.
Defective chargers: \(0.03(600) = 18\) from X and \(0.05(400) = 20\) from Y, so 38 in all.
The condition is “defective,” so the probability is \(\frac{20}{38} = \frac{10}{19}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is machine Y's share of all chargers (40%); it ignores the information that the charger is defective.
explanation.B: Correct. Of every 38 defective chargers, 20 come from machine Y, so the probability is \(\frac{20}{38} = \frac{10}{19}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{5}{3 + 5}\): it compares the two defect rates but ignores that machine X makes more chargers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the probability that a charger made by machine Y is defective (5%): the condition is reversed.

verify:
dx = Rational(60, 100) * Rational(3, 100)
dy = Rational(40, 100) * Rational(5, 100)
p = dy / (dx + dy)
assert p == Rational(10, 19)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
